CASMI 2026 training data analysis

Distributions of every training-relevant column in train.parquet, compared against the published test-set facts (timsTOF only, 10 adducts, mass 157–1,159 Da, 1–16 spectra per molecule, precursor+2 Da peak cut, base peak ≥ 1,000). Groups: enveda-180, enveda-np-examples (test-like), public libraries.

01Library sizes

enveda-180 is 45% of all spectra and 66% of all structures, but it is synthetic screening chemistry. The only instrument-and-pipeline-matched natural products are the 1,151 spectra in enveda-np-examples.

For training: Do not let enveda-180 dominate a loss by sheer count: weight or sample per library, or per structure.

02Spectra per structure

Median 6 spectra per structure overall (max 1,468). Within a library, enveda-np-examples has a median of 4, close to the test median of 3 (range 1–16). enveda-180 clusters at 4 and 8, its fixed CE/adduct grid.

For training: Aggregate per molecule as the test does. Cap spectra per structure during training so a few heavily measured compounds don't dominate.

03Structure overlap between libraries

90% of the 275,810 structures appear in only one library. All 250 np-examples structures also appear elsewhere (98% in RIKEN, 93% in GNPS). enveda-180 and spectraverse barely overlap anything.

For training: Split by InChIKey14 across all libraries, never by spectrum, or the same compound leaks into validation. The np-examples structures give a cross-instrument comparison: timsTOF vs Orbitrap/QTOF spectra of the same molecule.

04Mass

99% of training structures fall inside the test mass range (157–1,159 Da). Medians line up: 330 (enveda-180), 354 (np-examples), 349 (public) vs 348 in test. Some precursor_mz values are clearly broken (up to 2.4M).

For training: Mass coverage is fine. Drop the few absurd precursor_mz rows (ppm error flags them).

05Adducts

121 distinct adducts; 86% of spectra use one of the 10 test adducts. Dimers ([2M+Na]+, [2M+H]+, [2M-H]-) are big and absent from test. enveda-180 is 29% non-test adducts. RIKEN is unusually [M+Na]+-heavy.

For training: Filter to the 10 test adducts (or use them as a conditioning input). [M+H]+ and [M-H]- dominate, so rarer test adducts like [M+Cl]- and [M-H2O-H]- will be data-poor.

06Ionization mode and instrument

75% positive / 25% negative. Only enveda-180 and enveda-np-examples are timsTOF. 82 raw instrument strings collapse into ~6 families; drug_plus has no instrument at all.

For training: If a model takes instrument as input, use a grouped family, not the raw string. For domain adaptation the only in-domain pair is enveda-180 (chemistry mismatch) and np-examples (tiny).

07Collision energy

GNPS, drug_plus and masaryk have no CE at all; spectraverse is 92% missing. Pluskal is entirely NCE, so its eV is an approximate conversion. enveda-180 sits on a 20/40/60 eV grid. np-examples adds 35 and 80 eV and is 35% merged multi-energy spectra (e.g. '20;50', '20;40;60;80').

For training: Treat CE as optional with a 'missing' token rather than dropping 13% of spectra. Make sure the model handles merged multi-energy spectra, because the test set has them.

08Peak counts

Raw median 42 peaks, max 73,318. After the test-style cleaning (drop > precursor+2 Da) and a 1% floor the median is 13. 21% of spectra end up with fewer than 6 peaks and 20% have peaks above the precursor. That's 25% of enveda-180 and 42% of MoNA, all of which the test set removes.

For training: Always apply the test's precursor+2 Da cut to training data. Use top-N (~128) truncation: only 2% exceed 128 peaks after cleaning.

09Peak-level distributions

Public libraries have a hard floor at 1% intensity (already filtered upstream), while timsTOF spectra keep peaks down to 1e-5: 92% of enveda-180 peaks and 80% of np-examples peaks are below 1%. All groups have a precursor spike at ratio 1.0.

For training: Apply the same intensity floor to every library, or a model can tell the source library apart from noise density alone. A 1% floor is the simplest common denominator.

10Label quality and signal

Median |ppm error| is 1.5. RIKEN is noisy (27% > 10 ppm); Pluskal has about 10% of spectra beyond 100 ppm (likely wrong-adduct labels). base_peak_intensity is null for 46% of spectra; in GNPS, 31% of values are exactly 100 (pre-normalised, not raw counts).

For training: Use |ppm| ≤ 10 as a label-cleaning filter. Don't apply the test's base-peak ≥ 1,000 rule to GNPS values of 100/999. np-examples has the highest spectral entropy (richest spectra).

11m/z precision

np-examples stores 5–7+ decimals (raw floats); most public libraries store 4, RIKEN and MS-DIAL often 3 or fewer, and a few spectra are integer m/z.

For training: Bin or tolerance-match at ≥ 0.01 Da so low-precision libraries don't add noise. Formula annotation needs the high-precision libraries.

12Chemical space (Van Krevelen)

enveda-180 is confined to O/C < 0.5, the drug-like region. np-examples spreads to higher O/C (glycosides, polyphenols), which public libraries cover and enveda-180 doesn't.

For training: Natural-product test molecules lie partly outside enveda-180's chemical space. Public libraries are needed for O-rich chemistry even though they come from other instruments.

13Elements and unsaturation

enveda-180: 100% contain N, 35% halogenated, 0% CHO-only. np-examples: 47% N, 5% halogen, 52% CHO-only. Spectraverse is 30% P (lipids). DBE medians match (9), but np-examples has a longer tail.

For training: Any formula or element prior learned on enveda-180 will over-predict N and halogens for natural products. Reweight toward CHO-heavy chemistry.

14Test-like training subset

Test adduct → |ppm| ≤ 10 → base peak ≥ 1,000 (sentinels kept) → ≥ 6 cleaned peaks leaves 1.67M spectra and 263k structures (95% of structures). Also requiring a known CE drops to 1.43M / 232k.

For training: These filters cost spectra but almost no structures. A reasonable default training set.

15Missing values

Only five columns have nulls. base_peak_intensity is missing for whole libraries, and CE for GNPS, drug_plus and masaryk.

For training: Missingness is per library, not random. If the model sees a missing flag it can learn which library a spectrum came from, so check for that leak.
